title: NOT NULL Constraints & Safe Migrations
description: Enforce required fields with NOT NULL, avoid locking high-traffic tables when adding NOT NULL, and use NOT VALID.

data.text: The **`NOT NULL`** constraint ensures that a column cannot contain `NULL` values. While straightforward on new tables, adding a `NOT NULL` constraint to an existing billion-row table acquires an exclusive table lock while scanning all existing rows, causing downtime.

To safely add a `NOT NULL` constraint on high-traffic production tables, add a `CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID` constraint (which takes an instantaneous lock without scanning), validate it concurrently, and then enforce it.

data.title: Safe Migration Steps
data.content: Adding non-null constraint without locking the table.
data.code:
-- Step 1: Add check constraint marked as NOT VALID (instantaneous lock)
ALTER TABLE users 
ADD CONSTRAINT chk_users_phone_not_null 
CHECK (phone IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;

-- Step 2: Validate the constraint concurrently without blocking writes
ALTER TABLE users 
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT chk_users_phone_not_null;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `NOT NULL` enforces required values at the engine level.
Adding `NOT NULL` directly scans the entire table under an exclusive lock.
Use `CHECK ... NOT VALID` followed by `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` for zero-downtime migrations.
